root_idea.summary: A firm hold or strength in a thing, extending to possession, control, authority, and sovereignty.
root_idea.development: The root's basic notion of strength and firmness develops into having a secure hold over property or affairs, exercising power and rule, and designating kingship, ownership, and related realms of dominion.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Presented under the active-participial citation form مَالِك.
The single occurrence is a proper name, Mālik, rather than an independently evidenced lexical use of the active participle.
Displayed as the singular noun مَلَك.
The single مَلِيك occurrence belongs to the documented king/sovereign semantic branch and is subsumed under مَلِك rather than given an unsupported separate sense.
Displayed separately as مَلْك, the vocalized form attested in the Quranic reading of 20:87.
Normalized to the passive-participial citation form مَمْلُوك.

senses.definition: To possess or own; to hold something under one's control.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ and related expressions, the object is a person under ownership; the verb is otherwise general and is not restricted to persons or property.

senses.definition: To have power or capacity over something; to be able to affect or dispose of it.
senses.usage_conditions: Often used with benefit, harm, life, death, resurrection, or another outcome; this use denotes capability or effective control rather than simple possession.

senses.definition: To exercise command or rule over an affair or a people.
senses.usage_conditions: The construction may concern the ordering of an affair or the exercise of dominion over people, emphasizing governing authority.

senses.definition: Owner, possessor, or master: one who possesses something and has disposal or authority over it.
senses.usage_conditions: Can designate human ownership or mastery and divine ownership and authority; it may occur in relation to a thing, a realm, or an affair.

senses.definition: An angel; a single member of the angelic beings.
senses.usage_conditions: The singular denotes one angel, while مَلَائِكَة refers to angels collectively or in the plural; Quranic compounds also include the angel of death.

senses.definition: God's dominion or kingdom: the encompassing realm of divine sovereignty over creation.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage it is associated especially with the heavens and earth and with recognition of God's comprehensive authority.

senses.definition: King or sovereign: one who exercises command and prohibition over a people.
senses.usage_conditions: The lexical focus is governance and political or sovereign authority, not mere possession; the Quran applies the title to human kings and to God as sovereign.

senses.definition: Possession, authority, or the effective hold by which something is controlled.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic reading بِمَلْكِنَا, the expression means by our possession or authority; this vocalization is distinct from مِلْك and مُلْك.

senses.definition: Dominion, sovereignty, kingship, or rule: authority and power to command and dispose over a realm or what is governed.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses it for divine universal dominion as well as human kingship and rule; context may render it kingdom, dominion, sovereignty, or kingship.

senses.definition: A person owned as a slave; a bondperson.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is a passive participle describing a human subject to ownership; it does not itself impose a gender restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone possess a thing, or to make someone king and grant dominion, kingship, or rule.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes making a person responsible for the ordering of an affair as well as conferring possession or kingship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To knead dough thoroughly and make its kneading firm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with dough as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take possession of something, absolutely or by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form emphasizes acquisition of possession, including forcible acquisition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To restrain oneself from doing something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs especially in the negative idiom مَا تَمَالَكَ أَنْ فَعَلَ, meaning that one could not restrain oneself from acting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Owned property, especially houses and lands.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional usage of مِلْك includes real property and possessions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: God's world of spirits or the invisible world.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized theological usage distinguished from the apparent realm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The apparent or manifest dominion, especially the earthly realm when contrasted with مَلَكُوت.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This distinction is a Classical usage of مُلْك versus the less visible or spiritual realm.
A separate homonymous Classical meaning, unrelated to the angelic noun in sense.
A conventional superlative-style title for the supreme king or ruler.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The foundation, support, cause, or means by which an affair subsists and is ordered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to what an affair depends upon for its maintenance, order, or governance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The great master or owner, especially God, contrasted with the lesser human owner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional distinction between divine supreme ownership and ordinary human ownership.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A heron or a species of long-necked, long-legged bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized bird name and a homonymous lexical use of مَالِك.
An idiomatic expression rather than the ordinary owner or master meaning of مَالِك.
A specialized plural referring to bridal property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A faculty or firmly rooted quality of mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A settled mental disposition or ability, not possession in the ordinary material sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slave or bondperson; a synonym of مَمْلُوك.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This Classical form is vocalized مِلِيك and is distinct from the Quranic مَلِيك subsumed under the king/sovereign headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kingdom or realm: the sultanate of a king and the regions under his possession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Denotes the realm or territorial domain rather than the ruler himself.

cautions: The proper-name occurrence Mālik at 43:77 is excluded from the lexical form list and is not conflated with مَالِك, owner or master.
مَلَك meaning angel and the Classical homonym مَلَك meaning water are distinct lexical branches.
The Quranic مَلِيك occurrence is subsumed under the king/sovereign branch of مَلِك; the Classical مِلِيك meaning slave is a different vocalization and meaning.
